title: sb_join.py's CLICK_JS and body-text extraction only see the top document — Zoom's web-client join UI (name field, Join button, Join Audio by Computer, waiting-for-host, end-of-webinar text) renders inside a same-origin <iframe> that is never traversed
evidence: Live probe 2026-09-25 against the real Ashoka Educator Dialogues Zoom webinar join URL (raw/webinars/2026-09-27-ashoka-join-url.txt). After the bot's own autonomous 'join from browser' click (top-document button, matched fine), the top document at app.zoom.us/wc/95194691654/join has exactly ONE element ('Back'); DevTools shows a same-origin iframe with src identical to that URL. Confirmed via Selenium frame-switch: the iframe's actual content (e.g. this webinar's 'Sign in to join this meeting' screen) is invisible to CLICK_JS's document.querySelectorAll(...) and to the document.body.innerText read used for END_PHRASES/RECONNECT_PHRASES in sb_join.py's main() loop. packages/meeting-bot/py/sb_join.py CLICK_JS (top of file) and the body = sb.execute_script("return document.body...") line inside main()'s while loop are the exact spots. Screenshot: qa/evidence/u0-zoom-browser-join-2026-09-25/03-web-client-iframe-sign-in-required.png.
reproduction: python packages/meeting-bot/py/sb_join.py <a real zoom /w/ or /wc/ URL> --profile <dir> --title probe --stop-file <path>; observe the 'clicked' events stop after the initial top-document button, and any END_PHRASES/RECONNECT_PHRASES never fire even when the iframe visibly shows matching text
fix_direction: Make CLICK_JS and the body-text read iframe-aware: for each same-origin <iframe> (try/catch around .contentDocument access to skip cross-origin ones silently), also search its querySelectorAll(...) / innerText and merge with the top document's. Needs a live Zoom session past its own auth/consent screen to verify end-to-end (blocked by ISS-U0-2 today) — do not ship this fix without live verification per this repo's D-015/D-020 measurement discipline.

title: HUMAN_GATE — the Ashoka Educator Dialogues Zoom webinar (2026-09-27) requires participants to be signed in with a Zoom account; the bot has no Zoom credentials anywhere, so it cannot join past the web client's auth wall regardless of any code fix
evidence: Live probe 2026-09-25: after the bot's autonomous click reaches app.zoom.us/wc/95194691654/join, the web-client iframe shows 'Sign in to join this meeting — The host requires participants to be signed in with a Zoom account.' (screenshot: qa/evidence/u0-zoom-browser-join-2026-09-25/03-web-client-iframe-sign-in-required.png). Checked: navigating the SAME bot profile to zoom.us/profile redirects to zoom.us/signin#/login — no Zoom account is signed in on data/bot-profile/. Grepped .env and the whole repo for zoom_email/zoom_password/zoom_account — zero hits. No credential exists to fabricate or guess.
reproduction: python packages/meeting-bot/py/sb_join.py <the real ashoka join URL> --profile data/bot-profile --title probe --stop-file <path>; observe it reaches app.zoom.us/wc/.../join and stops there — no further progress is possible without an authenticated Zoom session
fix_direction: Needs an Approver decision (Umesh), not a code fix: (a) sign the bot's persistent Chrome profile into a Zoom account that matches (or the host will accept as) the approved registrant, and record how/where that credential is stored, OR (b) ask the Ashoka host to disable 'require authentication to join' for this webinar's registrants. Until one of those happens, T-024b/U0 cannot deliver a real recording of THIS webinar regardless of ISS-U0-1's fix.

title: Live-probe evidence: screenshots 02-after-autonomous-click-top-frame.png and 03-web-client-iframe-sign-in-required.png are byte-identical (same MD5 e2b5e6452be0937d3e4d17fd03f18e43), despite being captioned as two different DOM-state captures (top document with just a 'Back' link vs. the iframe's 'Sign in to join this meeting' dialog)
evidence: checker re-derivation 2026-09-25: `md5sum qa/evidence/u0-zoom-browser-join-2026-09-25/02-*.png qa/evidence/u0-zoom-browser-join-2026-09-25/03-*.png` -> identical hash; `cmp` confirms byte-identical. This means ISS-U0-1's own evidence text claim ("the top document at app.zoom.us/wc/95194691654/join has exactly ONE element ('Back')") has no distinct supporting screenshot -- only the prose assertion and the DOM-count claim back it, not image 02 as captioned. The canonical sb_join_live_events.jsonl and screenshot 03 are unaffected and remain accurate; this does not change the u0-zoom-browser-join unit's graded-criteria evidence (C1/C2/C10), which do not depend on distinguishing these two images.
fix_direction: The companion screenshot script likely screenshots the full composited viewport regardless of frame target, so it cannot visually distinguish 'top document only' from 'iframe content' when the iframe covers the page -- either drive/screenshot a specific frame context (Selenium switch_to.frame) for a genuinely distinct top-document capture, or drop the redundant 02 file and rely on the DOM element-count assertion (already in ISS-U0-1's evidence text) plus screenshot 03 alone.

title: CLICK_JS's visibility guard is not frame-aware: a same-origin iframe collapsed to zero size (width:0;height:0) still gets its contents clicked, because the guard reads the element's own getBoundingClientRect relative to its own document, never the ancestor <iframe>'s size/visibility in the parent document
evidence: checker-unit adversarial fixture (D:/KnowledgeBase-lanes/u0-zoom-iframe, u0-zoom-iframe-traversal cycle 1): a same-origin iframe with style="width:0;height:0;border:0;overflow:hidden;" containing a matching "Join" button, driven with real headless Chrome (SeleniumBase) against the unmodified packages/meeting-bot/py/sb_join.py CLICK_JS/JOIN_TEXTS (imported directly, never copied). sb.execute_script(CLICK_JS, JOIN_TEXTS) returned "join" (the button was clicked) despite the containing iframe rendering nowhere on the page. sb_join.py:49-97 (_IFRAME_WALK_JS / CLICK_JS), the r.width===0||r.height===0 guard inside the walkFrames visitor. This is a NEW failure mode introduced by the u0-zoom-iframe-traversal unit's frame recursion -- the prior top-document-only code had no way to reach content inside any collapsed container.
reproduction: local HTML fixture with a same-origin iframe style="width:0;height:0;border:0;overflow:hidden;" whose body contains a button matching JOIN_TEXTS; sb.execute_script(CLICK_JS, JOIN_TEXTS) against packages/meeting-bot/py/sb_join.py's real CLICK_JS returns the matched text (click fires) instead of null
fix_direction: In _IFRAME_WALK_JS's walkFrames, before visiting/recursing into a frame's contentDocument, check the <iframe> element's OWN getBoundingClientRect (width>0 && height>0) and computed display in its PARENT document; skip the whole subtree (never visit, never click) when the frame itself is not visible. Re-test with a 0-size AND a display:none iframe, both containing a matching button, asserting CLICK_JS returns null for both.

title: BODY_TEXT_JS merges text from an invisible same-origin iframe (display:none OR zero-size) into the END_PHRASES/RECONNECT_PHRASES check with no visibility gate at all, and this genuinely propagates to record-commands.ts's early-stop-on-'ended' logic
evidence: checker-unit adversarial fixture (D:/KnowledgeBase-lanes/u0-zoom-iframe, u0-zoom-iframe-traversal cycle 1): a same-origin iframe with style="display:none" (and, separately, width:0;height:0) containing the text "The webinar has ended. Thank you for attending.", driven with real headless Chrome against the unmodified packages/meeting-bot/py/sb_join.py BODY_TEXT_JS/END_PHRASES. sb.execute_script(BODY_TEXT_JS) merged that hidden text into the returned body string; next((p for p in END_PHRASES if p in body), None) matched "webinar has ended" for BOTH the display:none and zero-size cases. sb_join.py:99-115 (BODY_TEXT_JS) and :313 (the END_PHRASES match) feed packages/meeting-bot/src/capture/record-commands.ts:118 (endedAt set on first 'ended' event) and :168 (breaks the recording loop once now - endedAt > 60_000 AND now >= endNotBefore) -- the 60s+endNotBefore guard delays but does not prevent an early stop if a hidden DOM node with matching text persists for the whole run (e.g. a pre-rendered hidden end-of-meeting template, or a collapsed chat/waiting-room panel echoing a viewer's own message), which is a plausible real-Zoom SPA pattern this fixture set was not built to rule out.
reproduction: local HTML fixture with a same-origin iframe (display:none or width:0;height:0) whose body text contains an END_PHRASES substring (e.g. 'webinar has ended'); sb.execute_script(BODY_TEXT_JS) against packages/meeting-bot/py/sb_join.py's real BODY_TEXT_JS includes that text in its merged output
fix_direction: Same ancestor-frame-visibility gate as ISS-U0-4, applied to BODY_TEXT_JS: skip merging a frame's body text (and by extension RECONNECT_PHRASES/OFFLINE_PAGE_PHRASES detection) when the frame element itself is not visible in its parent document.
